title: Manufacturing Anomaly Detection — Deployment Proposal and Engagement Pricing
body:
Executive summary:

This document is a customer-facing deployment proposal and internal pricing sketch for a pilot-to-production engagement to deliver an on-premise / VPC-hosted anomaly-detection inference stack for mid-sized discrete manufacturing customer Acme Fabrication (placeholder name). Goal: detect equipment anomalies from vibration + audio + PLC telemetry at near-edge (<200ms) latency, provide model-inference endpoints for the MES, and create a production rollout path with predictable cost and operational SLAs.

Why Redwood is a fit (brief):
- Unified runtime that runs on dedicated GPU pools and private deployments — allows same API/rollouts across pilot and prod.
- Smart batching + KV/prefix caching reduces per-token cost for recurrent short sequences (sensor windows).
- Routing policies enable fallback from the most accurate heavy model to a smaller quantized variant when capacity is constrained.

High-level scope and deliverables (pilot -> prod):
1) Discovery (2 weeks) — on-site workshop + data review
   - Two-day workshop with engineering, OT, and IT to map data sources (vibration sensors, edge gateways, PLC tags).
   - Deliverable: data inventory, label availability, constraints (network, encryption), acceptance metrics (precision/recall thresholds, detection latency SLO).

2) Pilot (6 weeks) — model onboarding + local evaluation
   - Provision Redwood Private (customer VPC) with a small dedicated pool (1 x A10 + 1 x A10 backup) for pilot.
   - Ingest anonymized historical telemetry (up to 500k sensor windows) to run offline evals.
   - Onboard two candidate models (large accuracy-focused model + quantized low-latency variant).
   - Deliverable: pilot report with benchmarked accuracy, latency (P50/P95), cost per inference, and recommended tuning.

3) Validation (4 weeks) — live shadow inference + feedback loop
   - Deploy inference to edge gateway proxies; run shadow traffic for up to 3 production lines.
   - Implement simple feedback capture (operator labels through UI or CSV).
   - Deliverable: validation metrics, rollout plan, retraining/ops guidance.

4) Production rollout (8–12 weeks) — phased production
   - Capacity sizing and dedicated pool expansion, SLA definitions, runbooks, alerts integration (PagerDuty).
   - A/B rollout and automatic fallback rules configured in Redwood Console.
   - Handover packet: runbooks, monitoring dashboards, model versioning policy, incident playbooks.

Assumptions (critical):
- Customer will provide anonymized historical telemetry and connectivity to one test production line for shadowing.
- Customer networks allow outbound TLS to Redwood control plane from a bastion host (required for private control plane ops) or provide equivalent proxy.
- Licensing for any third-party edge gateways or OT connectors is customer's responsibility.
- Acceptance criteria are agreed after discovery; pilot success defined as meeting target F1 >= 0.78 and P95 inference latency <200ms for the quantized variant under pilot load.

Proposed deployment architecture (summary):
- Private control plane in customer VPC (Redwood Private).
- Dedicated inference pool inside customer subnet using customer-provided GPU nodes (option A) OR Redwood-managed dedicated capacity inside customer VPC (option B).
- Edge gateway proxies at factory floor aggregate sensor windows and forward preprocessed payloads (gzip JSON batches) to local inference endpoints over mTLS.
- Observability: token-level latency/cost breakdowns sent to Redwood Console, traces routed to customer Datadog instance, metrics to Prometheus/Pushgateway where requested.

Data handling and security notes:
- All PHI/PII: none expected. Telemetry will be anonymized — fields with operator IDs must be hashed prior to sharing.
- KMS integration: recommended for production (customer KMS) — include in Private deployment quote.
- Audit logs: audit export to S3 (or internal object store) for 90-day retention (extendable).

Risk and mitigations:
- OT network restrictions: plan for an on-site proxy/bastion and schedule network test in week 0.
- Label scarcity: propose small manual labeling sprint (10–20 hours operator time) during discovery and active learning loop in validation.
- Unexpected latency at 200ms SLO: validate with quantized model and implement deterministic batching window policy or route to local edge device for critical alerts.

Engagement pricing (draft figures, for discussion):
- Professional Services (time & materials, estimate):
  * Discovery workshop (2 engineers, 2 days on-site + prep): 40 hours @ $275/hr = $11,000
  * Pilot implementation (model onboarding, infra setup, evals): 6 weeks, 3 engineers (avg) 360 hours @ $225/hr = $81,000
  * Validation and tune (remote, 4 weeks): 160 hours @ $225/hr = $36,000
  * Production rollout support and runbooks: 180 hours @ $225/hr = $40,500
  * Project PM across engagement (fixed): $12,000
  * Contingency buffer (15%): $26,250
  Estimated total PS: $206,750

- Infra & software (monthly, piloting vs production):
  * Pilot Redwood Private (small): one-time provisioning & setup fee $6,000 + monthly managed private fee $4,500/mo (includes control plane + 1 A10 equivalent capacity).
  * Production dedicated capacity (example): 3 x A100-equivalent reserved pool (monthly committed): $40,000/mo or buydown for annual commit.
  * Optional: Extended observability retention + compliance package: $2,000/mo.

- Licensing & add-ons:
  * Model tuning & custom model license (if customer requests a Redwood-trained model): fixed $35,000 (optional).
  * On-prem appliance support (24x7) add-on: $8,000/mo.

Payment and contracting note:
- Typical structure: 40% on signature, 30% at pilot acceptance, 30% at production handover.
- PS work can be firm-fixed for discovery + pilot; subsequent phases T&M with capped estimate upon mutual agreement.

Workshop agenda (two-day discovery):
Day 1 — Stakeholders + Data
- 09:00 intro, goals, success metrics
- 10:00 OT/IT mapping: sensors, gateways, PLCs, data schemas
- 11:30 security & network constraints walkthrough
- 13:00 lunch
- 14:00 data quality deep-dive (sample windows, labeling)
- 15:30 success metrics & acceptance criteria
- 16:30 next steps and action items

Day 2 — Architecture & Ops
- 09:00 high-level infra options (private control plane, dedicated pools, edge hybrid)
- 10:30 integration points (MES, CMMS, alerting)
- 12:00 lunch
- 13:00 monitoring, incident response, SLA expectations
- 15:00 pilot timeline and responsibilities
- 16:00 sign-off on pilot scope and data handoff checklist

Customer-prep checklist (pre-work items):
- Provide sample anonymized telemetry (min 30k windows) and simple data dictionary
- Identify single line for pilot shadowing + contact for plant network
- Confirm KMS or indicate intent to use Redwood-managed key for pilot
- Grant temporary access window for network tests (week 0)

Acceptance criteria (pilot):
- F1 score >= 0.78 on historical labeled set OR precision >= 0.83 with recall >= 0.70 (business selects metric during discovery)
- P95 endpoint latency <200ms for quantized variant under pilot traffic profile
- Successful bi-directional trace export to customer monitoring (sample traces visible)

Next steps (recommended):
- Approve discovery workshop date (propose 2025-09-15) and sign mutual NDA if required.
- Kickoff ticket (JIRA ENG-1842) to be created and assigned to SE lead (Maya Thompson).
- Internal cost review and optional discount for multi-year infra commit to finance.

Open questions for discovery:
- Does the plant have an OT DMZ/Bastion that can host the Redwood agent?
- What is expected retention window for telemetry and model inference logs?
- Are there regulatory constraints (ISO27001, NERC) beyond standard manufacturing compliance?

Notes & rough timeline:
- Total elapsed time from discovery to first production line: 4–5 months (with parallel workstreams).
- Roadmap options: expand to NLP-based operator logs ingestion (future phase) and cross-line model federated updates.

Document owner and contact:
- Jordan Rivera (SE lead) — jordan.rivera@redwood.com — primary contact for proposal clarifications.

Revision history:
- 2025-08-06: initial draft
- 2025-08-22: pricing and pilot infra numbers updated after SRE consult
- 2025-09-02: added workshop agenda and tightened acceptance criteria
